 1
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice V. Gopala Krishna Rao

Judgment:

entities.text: M. Pankajakshi And Another vs M. Sudarshan Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants are claimants in M.V.O.P.No.890 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- Family Court -cum- Addl. District and Sessions Judge, at Anantapur, and the respondents herein are the respondents in the said case.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- Family Court -cum- Addl. District and Sessions Judge, at Anantapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The Claimants filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of MV Act, for claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of V. Suresh Babu (herein in after referred to as 'the deceased') in a Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 26.09.2008 at 04:30 P.M.
4.

The case of the petitioners are as follows:
On 26.09.2008 at about 04:30 p.m., and near Mushkin Vall Darga on Gooty-Guntakal Road, one V. Suresh Babu, who is the husband of the 1st petitioner,
father of 2nd petitioner and MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 son of 3rd respondent was proceeding along with others in the auto bearing registration No.AP 02 W 5206, lorry bearing registration No.AP 02 X 2049 belongs to 1st respondent and which was insured with the 2nd respondent being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed it due to which the deceased and another died at the spot itself and the police have registered a case against the driver of the lorry bearing No. AP 02 X 2049.
5.
The 1st respondent is remained ex parte.

6. The 2nd respondent filed a counter denying the material averments of the claim petition, and contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto driver, in which the deceased was travelling and also due to over load that contributory negligence must be attributed against the driver of the auto resulting the accident that the petition is bad due to non-impleading of the insurer and insured of the above auto and also the driver of the auto.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 1) Whether the accident occurred on 26.09.2008 at about 04:30 p.m., near Muskin Vali Darga, on Gooty-Guntakal Road, due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing No.AP 02 W 5206 and caused the death of the deceased?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from which respondent?
3
) To what relief?
8. The 1st petitioner has been examined as PW1 before the Tribunal.
The petitioners have examined two witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked Exs.A1 to Ex.A6 and marked Ex.X1.

on behalf of the 2nd respondent, no evidence is adduced, the 2nd respondent has marked Ex.B1 and B2.
9.

Basing on the material on record, the Tribunal held that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle lorry and awarded compensation of Rs.9,74,139/- together with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
Aggrieved by the same the present appeal is preferred by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

10. Now, the point for consideration are:
1) Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 2) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled enhancement of compensation as prayed for?

POINT NO. 1 & 2:
11.
In order to prove the claim of the petitioner, the 1st petitioner herself examined as PW1.

Though she stated in her evidence affidavit about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Vehicle, no importance will be given to her evidence because, she is not eye witness to the accident.
PW2 is the person who was travelling along with the deceased in the auto at the time of accident is best person to speak about the accident.

PW2 deposed in his evidence that in view of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 02 X 2049, the accident occurred and Motor Vehicles Inspector's report Ex.A4 establishes the accident is occurred not due any mechanical defects of the vehicle.

The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.A1 Certified copy of F.I.R.
and Ex.A5 certified copy of charge sheet
clearly pooves about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.AP 02 X 2049.

The learned Tribunal also gave the said finding against which no appeal preferred by the respondents, therefore, there is no need to M. Pankajakshi And Another vs M. Sudarshan Reddy And 2 Others on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157024082/
2 interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 12.

As per the case of the petitioners, the deceased was working as Secondary Garde Teacher, after giving cogent reasons on considering the evidence of PW3, Mandal Education Officer and Ex.A6 Salary Certificate, the learned Tribunal came to conclusion the deceased was earning salary Rs.7,935/- per month i.e., Rs.95,220/- per annum.
No appeal is filed by the respondents against the said finding.

Here the dependents on the deceased are 1st and 2nd petitioner and 3rd respondent mother, therefore 1/3rd income has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, after deducting 1/3rd amount, the contribution for the benefit of family members i.e., petitioners and third respondent is Rs.63.480/- per annum.
No appeal is also filed against the said finding.

13. As per the evidence of PW3/Mandal Education Officer coupled with Ex.X1 attested copy service register of deceased, the deceased was born on 01.07.1974 and the accident is taken place on 26.09.2008.
Therefore, the deceased was aged about 34 years by the date of accident.

As per decision of Smt. Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1, the multiplier applicable to the age group of the 2009 (4) SCJ 91 MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 deceased is '16'.

entities.text: Smt. Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the learned Tribunal applied the multiplier of 14.81, the said finding of the learned Tribunal is set aside, therefore Rs.63,480x16=Rs.10,15,680/- loss of consortium is awarded to the 1st petitioner is Rs.30,000/- because she lost her husband at young age, Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses of the deceased,
therefore in total the claimants are entitled compensation of Rs.10,65,680/-.
The Tribunal gave a finding that the 3rd respondent is entitled an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards her compensation.
No appeal is filed by the 3rd respondent against the said finding.

Here the enhanced amount of compensation is Rs.91,541/- (Rs.10,65,680-Rs.9,74,139/-)
14.

Therefore, the award dated 23.09.2009 passed in M.V.O.P.No.890 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- Family Court-cum-Addl. District and Sessions Judge, at Anantapur is modified to the extent as stated above.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- Family Court-cum-Addl. District and Sessions Judge, at Anantapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
15.. In the result appeal is allowed in part, enhancing the compensation from an amount Rs.
Rs.9,74,139/- to Rs.10,65,680/- with interest of 7.5% P.A. on enhanced MACMA.NO.1891 of 2012 compensation as awarded by the Tribunal against the respondents No.1 and 2.

Out of the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest, the 1st and 2nd petitioners are entitled to withdraw the equal share on the enhanced compensation amount with interest, the respondents 1 to 2 are directed to deposit the enhanced compensation Rs.91,541/- with interest within one (1) month from the date of the judgment.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V. GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J Dated:23.03.2023.
